question: A phone camera goes from 12 to 48 megapixels. How much finer can detail along one edge become?
answer: Up to twice as fine. Pixels fill an area, so four times as many means twice as many along each edge: 4,000 across becomes 8,000. Many 48-megapixel phone sensors also group pixels in fours under one colour filter and, in dim light, merge each group, handing back 12 megapixels anyway.
move: When a count covers an area, the gain along a line is its square root.
trap: Reading four times the pixels as four times the detail.
